sources.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes (arXiv:1907.09415)
sources.locator: Complete 239-page lecture-note PDF, sequentially read in the QA-r3 research run. This pair inspected §§7.1–7.2, printed pp.53–56 / PDF pp.65–68; local relevant text: research/quantum-algorithms-planning/sources/qa_r2/de-wolf-1907.09415.txt, lines 4451–4828.
sources.reading_verification: Inspected the complete local text of §§7.1–7.2, including the marked/unmarked plane, exact integer success law, integer-rounding bound, reflection-cost note, and the warning that the phase oracle is a rank reflection only on the two-dimensional good/bad plane.

contents.name: 7.1 finite search problem and solution count
contents.support: The source defines a finite Boolean search string and its number t of solutions; the local item fixes the ordered address encoding and standard bit/phase-oracle conventions.

contents.name: 7.2 phase oracle, Grover iterate, and query/gate separation
contents.support: The source writes the phase-query iterate and separates one oracle query from the other gates; the local bit-query implementation is supplied by the declared phase-kickback theorem.

contents.name: Good and bad uniform states and the initial angle
contents.support: The source decomposes the uniform vector into normalized marked and unmarked components with sine/cosine coefficients; the local proof checks orthonormality and angle ranges.

contents.name: Product of reflections and the invariant two-dimensional plane
contents.support: The source identifies the two reflections and derives the geometric good/bad plane; the source’s footnote caveat is retained in the local statement about the restricted action.

contents.name: Exact success probability after k integer iterations
contents.support: The source gives the (2k+1)θ state and the squared marked amplitude; the local proof also derives the measured address marginal over the response register.

contents.name: Known-count integer rounding and failure bound
contents.support: The source bounds failure after rounding the real optimum to a legal integer; the local proof spells out the floor/ceiling choice and query range.

contents.name: Known-count search query scale
contents.support: The source gives the O(sqrt(N/t)) query scale when t is known; the local theorem preserves the distinct verification query and explicitly excludes exact classical maximization work.

contents.name: Unknown-count search and the need for an increasing schedule
contents.support: The source flags overshooting and sketches an exponentially increasing iteration schedule; the local BBHT definition fixes c=3/2, direct sampling, verification, and the no-finite-empty-decision boundary.

contents.name: Source-adjacent empty-set detection assertion
contents.support: The source’s brief sentence about detecting an empty set is not imported: the local algorithm has no finite-time emptiness test, and the local proof records that it runs forever when t=0.
contents.reason: This sentence is not used because the local BBHT procedure does not halt at t=0 and no finite list of failed samples certifies emptiness in the unknown-count black-box model.

sources.title: Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms (17 April 2025)
sources.locator: Complete 191-page lecture-note PDF, sequentially read in the QA-r3 research run. This pair inspected §§19.1–19.3, printed pp.87–89 / PDF pp.95–98; local relevant text: research/quantum-algorithms-planning/sources/qa_r2/childs-lecture-notes.txt, lines 8148–8585.
sources.reading_verification: Inspected the complete local text of §§19.1–19.3. Section 19.1 gives the finite-set black-box search model and high-level Grover query bound; §§19.2–19.3 treat the related quantum-walk and amplitude-amplification/counting viewpoints.

contents.name: 19.1 finite-set unstructured search and query complexity
contents.support: The source provides an independent finite-set black-box formulation and query-complexity context; local notation fixes D_n, word-slot encoding, and the bit-query promise.

contents.name: 19.1 Grover search gives a square-root query bound
contents.support: The source states the high-level Grover search bound; its phase-oracle/query convention is not used to replace the local single standard-bit-query phase-kickback proof.

contents.name: 19.2 quantum-walk search on the complete graph
contents.support: This is a different algorithm and register model from the standard address-register Grover iterate commissioned on this page.
contents.reason: The quantum-walk construction and its two-query step are outside the assigned Grover/BBHT pair; no walk claim or resource count is imported.

contents.name: 19.3 general amplitude amplification and quantum counting
contents.support: The section supplies broad amplitude-amplification context; the local proof derives the finite integer-average identity and its 1/4 lower bound directly.

sources.title: Gilles Brassard, Peter Høyer, Michele Mosca, and Alain Tapp, Quantum Amplitude Amplification and Estimation (arXiv:quant-ph/0005055)
sources.locator: Complete 32-page paper, sequentially read in the QA-r3 research run. This pair inspected §2, especially the amplitude-amplification success law, Theorem 2, QSearch/Theorem 3 and its expected-cost proof sketch, PDF pp.6–9; local text: research/quantum-algorithms-planning/sources/qa_r3/bhmt-quant-ph-0005055.txt, lines 300–525.
sources.reading_verification: Inspected the complete relevant §2 derivation and QSearch proof sketch: the exact (2j+1)θ success law, known-success-probability choice, QSearch stage schedule, and expected-cost geometric argument. The local BBHT proof fills in the source’s stated sketch.

contents.name: Amplitude-amplification exact success law
contents.support: The source derives the exact sine-squared success probability for integer iterate count; local notation specializes its good/bad decomposition to finite marked-address search.

contents.name: Known success probability and quadratic-speedup theorem
contents.support: The source’s Theorem 2 provides a known-success-probability success guarantee; the local proof combines its exact law with the integer-regime lemma and the rational-list consistency proof.

contents.name: Unknown-probability QSearch stage schedule
contents.locator: §2, Theorem 3 and Algorithm QSearch, PDF pp.8–9
contents.support: The source’s QSearch algorithm uses direct sampling, uniformly selected iteration counts, and geometrically increasing stage sizes; the local version fixes c=3/2 and verifies every candidate.

contents.name: Expected-cost proof sketch for unknown-probability search
contents.support: The source gives the high-success/failure-tail split and a geometric expected-work sketch; the local theorem proves all stage and finite-prefix estimates in full.

canonical.name: Exact rational Chebyshev recurrence for selecting an integer iterate
canonical.support: Local extension: the source’s trigonometric success law is encoded by a rational recurrence; its recurrence identity, numerator bit lengths, exact comparisons, and exponential worst-case preprocessing are proved locally.

canonical.name: Fixed nine-round known-count randomization and its 2/3 guarantee
canonical.support: Local finite-round construction from the uniform integer-average lemma; rejection sampling and the nine-round failure estimate are proved in the assigned items.

canonical.name: Separate gate, classical-bit, and bit-query accounting
canonical.support: Local resource derivation using the repository cost definitions; the reflection implementation and verification query remain separate coordinates.

canonical.name: Complete BBHT stage lower bound and almost-sure termination
canonical.support: The source gives only a brief averaged-success sketch; this pair proves the finite trigonometric sum and the exact 3/8 stage bound, then uses it for almost-sure termination.

canonical.name: Finite-branch marginal needed to measure only the address register
canonical.support: The local proof sums the finite output law over the unmeasured response wire; this measurement convention is imported from the actual batch-25 supplier and checked in the cross-batch ledger.

contents.name: Exact t=N/4 example and first integer peak
